note: HAND-WRITTEN. This file is the independent oracle for contract rule C3 — the Python local path
dependency — and it was written BEFORE the resolver existed. It is never generated by running
Nerve, and no script writes it. If it were produced by the thing it grades, the precision
measurement over it would be Nerve agreeing with itself.
Every row below was read off fixtures/contracts-python/service/pyproject.toml by hand.
Declarations are keyed by (section, name), never by line number or repository id, for the reason
fixtures/contracts-npm/ground_truth.json gives: keying on anything only obtainable by running
the thing under test would make this file a derived artifact.
ONE PLACEHOLDER. PEP 621 direct references are absolute URLs, and an absolute path cannot be
committed — it would name the machine the fixture was built on, which CLAUDE.md §8 forbids and
crates/nerve-cli/tests/registry_guards.rs would fail on. The harness substitutes
{{PKG_CORE_PATH}} with the built pkg-core root before scanning. The substitution changes one
URL and nothing else; this file says what the answer is either way.
THIS TABLE IS NEVER SUMMED WITH C1's. Two rules, two tables, no combined number.

placeholder.replaced_with: the absolute path of the built pkg-core checkout
placeholder.before_substitution: file://{{PKG_CORE_PATH}} is not an absolute file URL, so the declaration is unsupported — python_unsupported_direct_reference

verdicts.link: this declaration must produce exactly one contract link, to the named target, with the named resolution_method.
verdicts.unresolved: the form is supported and fully understood, and it reaches no registered neighbour. No link, and the named reason reported.
verdicts.unsupported: a form Nerve declines to read. No link, and the form named in the tally.
verdicts.declined_true_link: the declaration names a registered neighbour by an explicit path and the form is outside the enumerated syntax. Nerve declines it, records it with the form named, and this file counts it as a FALSE NEGATIVE — 10b's `Views.handle` rule, applied to a second language so the miss means the same thing in both.

declarations.name: pkg-core
declarations.why: a PEP 621 direct reference to an absolute file URL. The URL is read as written — no percent-decoding, because a decoder of our own in the expression that chooses a directory is the trade T11 records this project refusing.

declarations.name: pkg-extra
declarations.why: a Poetry path dependency. `develop = true` changes how the package is installed and says nothing about which repository it is, so it is neither required nor read.

declarations.name: pkg-both
declarations.why: one identity declared in two tables, naming two different repositories. Both links are recorded and neither is promoted.

declarations.name: pkg-unregistered
declarations.why: the negative case for C3: a real, indexed, adjacent Nerve repository named by an explicit path still produces no link, because registration is explicit and nothing is auto-discovered.

declarations.name: pkg-rel
declarations.why: a file URL naming the sibling checkout, relatively. PEP 508 direct references are absolute, and resolving a relative one would mean deciding what it is relative to — the manifest, the project root, the working directory — which is a rule Nerve would be inventing. Declining it is a real miss and it is published as one rather than resolved by guessing.

declarations.name: flask
declarations.why: a bare name with no version at all is still a registry resolution, and 'flask' in two repositories may be two packages.

declarations.name: pkg-uv-ws
declarations.why: workspace = true names no path at all, so there is nothing to resolve without matching a package name against a directory — which is the fuzzy identity §1 refuses.
